notes: GPT subagents no longer die on a dead Aliax sign-in, and codex's own retries stop showing as error rows. Every codex thread since 2026-10-11 landed on landon@unifyplatforms.com, whose codex token answers 401 token_expired: chooseAccount (accountRouting.ts) ranks by 5h headroom and live threads, and an account nobody can use never spends, so it won every pick, while core's failover reacts to 429 only. AccountsService (accounts.ts) now keeps an out-set per provider: markOut on a 401 (new marks log once and mark the usage stale), markAnswered on any success, isOut for OUT_RETRY_MS (10 min, because Aliax's usage cache still reads the dead account as healthy and a standby never polls, so no snapshot can clear the mark; after the window one request tries it again and a second 401 marks it afresh while the gateway replays that request elsewhere), outFor also counting reports the snapshot flags expired, and substitute() picking the best account with room for a request whose account is out. chooseAccount takes `out`: no room, never a pick, so a pinned thread expects the fallback and a sticky thread leaves. Gateway.handle (gateway.ts) routes every scoped request through forwardScoped: the body is buffered, the host's substitute hook may rename the account before the request leaves (sent as a pin so core drops any 429 override it held), a 401 is held back by HeldResponse and the same bytes replay once under what onUnauthorized names, with nothing to name the 401 passes through as it came, and onRouted fires once per change so the thread's row follows (rescope rewrites the ~t=…;a=… segment on both the codex ports and the claude plain-port path). index.ts wires substitute/onUnauthorized/onResponse to the service and, when no account is left, registry.signInNeeded posts one error row "Aliax account X needs sign-in" naming the thread's own account and drops codex's "workspace routing discovery unauthorized (401)" rows for that thread until it lands elsewhere or a turn goes through. The "Reconnecting... n/5" rows were not the WebSocket refusal: a codex app-server pointed at a fake origin answering 401 shows them as codex's own retries of that 401 (willRetry: true) before the final error, with no upgrade attempt at all, and a healthy pinned thread in the dev instance shows one refused upgrade and no rows; drivers/codex.ts now logs such a retry once per turn instead of emitting a row, and the gateway's upgrade comment says what was measured. Tests: accountRouting (out), accounts (mark, lift, window, expired report, substitute), gateway (401 replay, straight-to-substitute, return, pass-through, rescope), codex driver (retries are a log line, the ending error a row), sessions-limits (signInNeeded once per account, wording dropped, lifted on a move or a good turn); scripts/e2e-gateway-unauthorized.ts runs the real service, gateway and registry against a fake upstream through the dead → substitute → nothing-left → recovered sequence. Verified in the isolated dev instance: a gpt-6-astra thread pinned to the healthy account answers OK with no error rows and one "upgrade refused" trace line.
